note: He closed, and he sits outside the stated ICP on three of the four criteria this recording can assess. Occupation is the clearest miss: the ICP names business owners, physicians 'or equivalent', and he is a serving US Army linguist who describes himself as 'all the way down at the company. I'm like bottom of the rung echelon wise'. That is a respected, skilled, institutionally salaried role and it is not the profile the ICP describes. Income fails on the same test the corpus already applied to Francisco Vega — he could not assemble $6,000 across a checking account and two credit cards, said so plainly ('I don't quite get to the $6,000'), and closed only via twelve-month third-party consumer credit. The nuance worth carrying to the rollup is that his monthly position is actually sound, $1,500 to $2,000 free with another $900 just released by the end of child support; what he lacks is liquidity, not income. Good-to-great fails because the entire buying logic is avoidance of decline rather than elevation from good — '$6,000 now, as opposed to how many thousands will I have to pay if my health just gets worse'. Neglected health is the one clean match. The fifth criterion, not_deconditioned, is genuinely unassessable here: this is a follow-up call with no baseline, no weight, no height and no training history, all of which sat on a first call that is not in this batch, so it is deliberately excluded from both lists rather than guessed at. This is now the second closed deal in the corpus that falls outside the stated ICP, after Robyn Stillwater, and it strengthens the existing observation that the buying population is materially wider than the ICP as stated on live calls.
